content.text:
I added `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. **It uploads `.vitest/junit/output.xml`** (relative to the repo root).

The workflow checks out the repo, sets up Node 22, runs `npm ci`, then runs `npx vitest run --reporter=default --reporter=junit`. That keeps the normal console output and also writes the JUnit report. No output file is configured anywhere, so Vitest uses its default location. `actions/upload-artifact@v4` then uploads the report as an artifact named `junit-report`. The upload runs even when tests fail, because that's when you most need the report. It's skipped only if the run is cancelled. If the file is missing, the upload step fails rather than passing silently.

I didn't take the path from the project's lessons note on trust; I checked it two ways:
- **Vitest 5.0.3 source:** when no output file is set, the JUnit reporter writes `output.xml` into `<root>/.vitest/junit/`.
- **Local run:** I ran the same command here. The one test passed and Vitest reported writing `.vitest/junit/output.xml`. I then deleted that local `.vitest` folder so it doesn't end up in the repo.

The workflow itself hasn't run on GitHub yet; this folder isn't a git repository, so there was nothing to push.

You may want to add `.vitest/` to `.gitignore` so local test runs don't commit the report.
